pinterest.title: Turkish Wedding Traditions in Order: From Kız İsteme to the Kına Gecesi and the Wedding Day
pinterest.description: Turkish wedding traditions follow an order: kız isteme, the formal asking for the bride's hand, then söz and nişan, the çeyiz (trousseau) and the kına gecesi, before the flag, the procession with davul and zurna and the marriage itself. Customs differ from region to region and family to family, so ask both families what they expect. Our guide marks what is sourced and what is only often told.

pinterest.title: What Happens at a Turkish Henna Night (Kına Gecesi)
pinterest.description: The kına gecesi is usually held at the bride's home on the night before the wedding, or a day or two before. Folk songs are sung, unmarried girls circle the bride holding candles, and henna is applied to her palm. When she keeps her hand closed, the mother-in-law places a gold coin in it as a henna gift. A Turkish wedding traditions guide for couples planning with both families.

pinterest.title: Turkish Coffee at the Asking: A Turkish Wedding Tradition UNESCO Recognises
pinterest.description: At kız isteme, the groom's family formally asks the bride's family for her hand, and coffee is part of the occasion. UNESCO listed Turkish coffee culture and tradition in 2013 and says it plays an important role on social occasions such as engagement ceremonies. The salted cup for the groom? Often told, but we found no cultural or academic source for it. More Turkish wedding traditions, in order, in our guide.

slides: A Turkish wedding is rarely one day. Here are the traditions, in order.
1. Kız isteme: the groom's family formally asks the bride's family for her hand. Coffee is part of the occasion, and UNESCO says Turkish coffee plays an important role at engagement ceremonies.
2. Söz and nişan: the families' agreement and the engagement. In Hatay, a small gathering is called söz kesimi and a larger one nişan.
3. Çeyiz: the trousseau prepared for the new home, often laid out for relatives to see.
4. Kına gecesi: usually the night before the wedding, or a day or two before. Folk songs, candles, henna in the bride's palm and a gold coin from the mother-in-law.
5. The wedding day: a flag goes up at the wedding house, davul and zurna play, and the gelin alayı sets out to collect the bride.

Marrying legally in Türkiye? Applications go through a municipal marriage office (evlendirme dairesi), and the paperwork, including a certified eligibility certificate, should start well before you fly.

instagram_carousel.caption:
A Turkish wedding is rarely one day. It begins with a formal visit between two families and can pass through a promise, an engagement and a henna night before the music, the procession and the marriage itself.

Our guide follows Turkish wedding traditions in order, from kız isteme to the kına gecesi and the wedding day, and marks which details are sourced and which are simply often told (yes, including the salted coffee).

Customs differ from region to region and family to family, so the best first step is asking both families which customs they want to keep, which they would happily skip, and who should lead each one.

For Australians marrying legally in Türkiye, we also cover the municipal marriage office, the documents one Istanbul office lists for foreign nationals and Smartraveller's advice as at November 2026.

Read the full guide via the link in our bio, and save this for when the families start talking dates. Planning with Turkish roots? Send us a message to speak with a Wedded Advisor.
